source.note: Official DBE November 2019 Mathematics P2 marking guidelines (English/Afrikaans). Bilingual PDF; English transcribed only.

extraction.method: transcription from the official PDF text layer, checked against 140 dpi page renders

notes: If a candidate answers a question TWICE, only mark the FIRST attempt. If a candidate has crossed out an attempt of a question and not redone the question, mark the crossed out version. Consistent accuracy applies in ALL aspects of the marking memorandum. Stop marking at the second calculation error. Assuming answers/values in order to solve a problem is NOT acceptable. A mark for a correct statement (a statement mark is independent of a reason) is indicated by S. A mark for the correct reason (a reason mark may only be awarded if the statement is correct) is indicated by R. Award a mark if statement AND reason are both correct (S/R).

$\mathrm{E}\hat{\mathrm{F}}\mathrm{D}=\mathrm{E}\hat{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{D}$ [proved in 8.2.1]

$E$, $F$, $C$ and $D$ are concyclic.

$\hat{O}_2=360^{\circ}-x$ [$\angle$s around a point]

$\therefore\hat{M}=180^{\circ}-\dfrac{1}{2}x$ [$\angle$ at the centre $=2\times\angle$ at the circumference]

$\therefore\hat{T}_2+\hat{P}_1=\dfrac{1}{2}x$ [sum of $\angle$s in $\Delta$]

$\therefore\hat{T}_2=\hat{P}_1=\dfrac{1}{4}x$ [$\angle$s opp. equal sides]

$\therefore\mathrm{S}\hat{\mathrm{T}}\mathrm{M}=\hat{P}_1=\dfrac{1}{4}x$ [tan-chord theorem]

steps.description: $\angle$ at the centre $=2\times\angle$ at the circumference

alternatives.label: OR
alternatives.working_md:
$\hat{O}_2=360^{\circ}-x$ [$\angle$s around a point]

$\therefore\hat{M}=\dfrac{1}{2}\hat{O}_2$ [$\angle$ at the centre $=2\times\angle$ at the circumference]

$\therefore\hat{T}_2+\hat{P}_1=180^{\circ}-\hat{M}$ [sum of $\angle$s in $\Delta$]

$\therefore\hat{T}_2=\hat{P}_1$ [$\angle$s opp. equal sides]

$=\dfrac{180^{\circ}-\hat{M}}{2}=\dfrac{180^{\circ}-\frac{1}{2}\hat{O}_2}{2}=\dfrac{180^{\circ}-\frac{1}{2}(360^{\circ}-x)}{2}=\dfrac{1}{4}x$

$\therefore\mathrm{S}\hat{\mathrm{T}}\mathrm{M}=\dfrac{1}{4}x$ [tan-chord theorem]

Construction: draw $h_1$ from $E$ perpendicular to $AD$ and $h_2$ from $D$ perpendicular to $AE$.

$\dfrac{\text{area }\Delta ADE}{\text{area }\Delta BDE}=\dfrac{\frac{1}{2}AD\cdot h_1}{\frac{1}{2}DB\cdot h_1}=\dfrac{AD}{DB}$

$\dfrac{\text{area }\Delta ADE}{\text{area }\Delta DEC}=\dfrac{\frac{1}{2}AE\cdot h_2}{\frac{1}{2}EC\cdot h_2}=\dfrac{AE}{EC}$

But area $\Delta BDE=$ area $\Delta DEC$ [same base and height, or $DE\parallel BC$]

$\therefore\dfrac{\text{area }\Delta ADE}{\text{area }\Delta BDE}=\dfrac{\text{area }\Delta ADE}{\text{area }\Delta DEC}$

$\therefore\dfrac{AD}{DB}=\dfrac{AE}{EC}$
